description.short: Dan Cong with a distinctive nutty ('almond') aroma, less floral than Mi Lan Xiang
description.overview: One of the Dan Cong aroma types dominated by nutty rather than floral notes — a vivid illustration of the diversity possible within a single terroir and processing craft.
description.taste: Nutty, mellow, with a full body and mineral foundation
description.processing: Classic Dan Cong craft: withering → shaking → kill-green → rolling → baking/roasting

history.origin: Named after its dominant aromatic note reminiscent of almonds — consistent with the tradition of naming all Dan Cong varieties by their distinctive fragrances.
history.development: Like other Fenghuang xiangxing (aroma types), it was developed through the selection of individual mother bushes with this unique aroma and propagated via cuttings.
history.modern: Less famous in the West than Mi Lan Xiang, but highly prized by connoisseurs for its atypical nutty rather than purely floral profile.
interestingFacts: The Fenghuang 'xiangxing' (aroma profile) system comprises more than ten officially recognized categories, and Xing Ren Xiang represents one of the less commercialized yet instantly recognizable styles.
